overall.judgement: Yes, this is worth reading for a mathematically trained reader seeking a careful map of candidate breakthroughs and the precise obstacles they purport to overcome. It now contains genuine synthesis and useful small mathematical controls. It is still less accessible and less natural than a strong interdisciplinary survey: several mechanism summaries assume specialist vocabulary, and repeated verification-oriented endings weaken the narrative payoff.
overall.naturalness: Professional, precise and mostly readable. Some passages feel assembled from domain reports rather than written around one reader's questions. That impression comes from repeated patterns of naming a proposed bridge, listing technical constructions, and ending with audit priorities; it is not a claim that prose style can determine authorship.
overall.length: The breadth can justify roughly 18 pages of discussion plus the source-rich bibliography. The current length is defensible, but 10–15% of generic method/verification repetition could be exchanged for short explanations of the few technical objects the argument actually needs. More citations or more case studies would not improve the paper at this stage.
overall.recommendation: Focused editorial revision, rather than another broad literature expansion. Prioritize explanatory entry points, a concrete reader promise in the introduction, and mathematical takeaways at case endings.
overall.distinction_from_prior_audit: The contrastive selection register, four-state control, amplification example, grid example, source-attribution fixes, and superlogarithmic-loss correction resolve the earlier specific concerns. They are not reopened here.

scores.reason: A reader gains a map of which additional compatibility or quantifier is doing the work, rather than merely learning that famous conjectures are claimed solved.
The four-state chain, duplicate-row square, characteristic-two cancellation, scalar/amplified norm distinction, and dyadic summability analysis make several comparisons memorable.
The input/property/quantifier/loss profile connects the cases without pretending their positivity notions are identical. The itinerary still needs a reader-facing preview before the specialist tours.

scores.category: Accessibility to a mathematically trained interdisciplinary reader
scores.reason: Jets, matroids/common bases, FPRAS, Unique Games, missing-slot transport and layer fields arrive with uneven explanation. A reader outside a case's field can often repeat the mechanism name without understanding the mathematical object.
Direct mathematical passages read well; recurring proposed-bridge and verification-target closures interrupt the exposition and make the sections feel templated.

The four-column table and comparisons with concurrent work clearly separate inherited ingredients from additional scope. Some section conclusions still list what to inspect instead of giving a concise authorial judgement about what would be new.
Theme-guided contrastive selection and the absence of a historical exhaustive omission list are now explicit. The paper makes claims about its selected cases rather than prevalence across the corpus.

Primary comparisons, fixed versions and explicit preprint status are strengths. The fresh source checks below support selected consequential contrasts; they do not establish comprehensive coverage or validate the released proofs.
The case breadth and bibliography justify the page count, but repeated methodology and source-binding detail compete with the explanations an interdisciplinary reader most needs.
The illustrative calculations are appropriately small and their inferential limits are clear. This score does not rate the correctness of the underlying breakthrough claims.

strongest_passages.value: The square with duplicate rows makes a representation-dependent probability multiplicity tangible. This is a strong example of why a geometric object and its indexed encoding are different.
The four-state chain gives an exact, reusable explanation of why selected-observable control does not imply a full spectral gap.

The signed impulse estimate is followed through to dyadic doubling times, and the generalized reciprocal-scale test shows exactly which loss budgets preserve the consequence. This teaches an argument rather than only locating one.
The scalar, small-base complete and arbitrary-dimensional complete scopes are compared, and classical similarity/attainment are separated from the proposed sharp bound.
The table-sampling discussion separates target law, precision dependence, exact law computation and expected branch cost. These distinctions have relevance beyond the source manuscript.

concrete_revision_text.location: research/combinatorics/section.tex, replace the opening paragraph of the Unique Games section; the following release theorem remains unchanged
concrete_revision_text.latex_text: A Unique Game assigns labels to the vertices of a constraint graph. Each edge carries a permutation, so fixing the label at one endpoint determines the label that satisfies that edge at the other. The value of the game is the largest fraction of edges satisfied by a labeling. Perfect satisfiability can be checked by propagating labels; the difficult regime is almost satisfiability: distinguishing value at least \(1-\varepsilon\) from value at most \(\delta\), for fixed positive errors \cite[Section~2.4]{FrontKhot2010}. The established shortcode and Grassmann-expansion line gives imperfect-completeness hardness \cite{FrontBKS2019,FrontKMS2023}. Ordinary repetition reduces completeness as well as soundness, so it does not by itself reach the near-one regime. The claimed advance in family102 is a gadget that changes this tradeoff; the downstream SDP-threshold framework is already available conditionally \cite{FrontRaghavendra2008}.
concrete_revision_text.primary_support: Khot's original author PDF, Definition2.4 and Conjecture2.5, pp.5–6; the immediately preceding discussion explains polynomial-time propagation when the optimum is exactly1.
concrete_revision_text.implementation_note: Use the existing FrontKhot2010 citation. No new bibliography item is needed. The text concerns the standard finite-alphabet constraint formulation, and does not claim that an almost-satisfiable instance can be decided by propagation.
concrete_revision_text.additional_short_entry_point: Before the arithmetic interpolation mechanism: 'A jet is a prescribed finite list of derivatives at a point. The interpolation step must meet many such prescriptions while controlling the polynomial degree and the later denominator cost. Its distinctive quantifier is that the weights are chosen before the approximation centres are known.' Expand FPRAS as 'fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme' at its first occurrence.

concrete_revision_text.location: main.tex, replace the final introduction paragraph beginning 'The case studies were selected for three reasons'; selection remains documented in the method
concrete_revision_text.latex_text: The review asks what would actually have to be new for these conclusions to follow. Exact table generation, for example, uses an earlier correction method; the proposed advance is computing the approximate sampler's law at a cost the rare correction can afford \citep{FrontGLMP2024}. Complete Crouzeix draws on established spectral-set and similarity methods; its additional burden is keeping the sharp constant independent of the matrix-coefficient dimension \citep{GOCrouzeixPalencia2017,GOPaulsen1984}. The remaining cases are read in the same way, separating the obstacle, the inherited route, and the additional estimate. Arithmetic and kinetic examples emphasize quantifiers and cancellation; convex and operator examples emphasize sharpness; counting and algebra emphasize what must be preserved when a representation changes. Table~\ref{tab:interfaces} collects the resulting novelty judgements.
concrete_revision_text.implementation_note: This replaces procedural material rather than adding another introductory paragraph. It keeps the current conditional source-result status and existing citations.

concrete_revision_text.location: synthesis.tex, replace the present conclusion with a shorter reader-facing takeaway; routine verification advice remains in the method and evidence package
concrete_revision_text.latex_text: The comparison locates three recurring sources of added scope: retaining information that an earlier estimate discards, changing a representation while preserving a precise property, and keeping a loss uniform across the required parameters. The examples show why each qualifier matters. A restricted energy estimate can survive when global mixing fails; a scalar norm argument can lose a matrix-dimension factor; a positive mesh can miss a negative value between its nodes. For exact tables, the proposed law evaluator carries the additional algorithmic burden; for common bases, selected transport must be sufficient together with trace and return control; for complete Crouzeix, the ordered estimates must survive arbitrary amplification. These narrower intermediate statements are the mathematical objects through which the candidate breakthroughs should be understood. Their reconstruction would distinguish new reusable estimates from new combinations of established machinery.
concrete_revision_text.implementation_note: This proposal retains conditionality without repeating the full audit workflow. It is not a new theorem, a performance assertion, or certification of the release.
